explanation:
For each divisor, choose a polar presentation using the already proved Riemann construction. Tuple-height comparison for equal local minimum orders proves invariance under principal divisors and addition. A divisor of positive degree has a positive multiple linearly equivalent to an actual polar divisor, so its chosen height is bounded below. Given $\deg E<q\deg D$ with $\deg D>0$, choose a rational number $a/b$ strictly between $\deg E/\deg D$ and $q$, with $b>0$. The divisor $aD-bE$ has positive degree. Its lower height bound, additivity and the multiple laws give an upper comparison for $h_E$ at coefficient $a/b$. The lower bound for $h_D$ raises that coefficient to $q$. Finally, compare both internally chosen heights with the two arbitrary supplied presentations. The error from multiplying by $q$ is bounded using $|q|$, so every real $q$ remains allowed. The result holds at every proper algebraic point, including poles, with the constant chosen independently of the point. This closes the exact divisor comparison leaf; the canonical-estimate parent retains its other open children.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.positiveDegreePolarRealization`

Let $N$ be any natural number and $M$ a model: its field $K$ is an intermediate field of an algebraic closure of $ℚ(T)$, with $u,v∈K$, $u$ transcendental over $ℚ$, $u^N+v^N=1$, $ℚ(u,v)=K$, and $K/ℚ(u)$ finite-dimensional of degree $N$. A place is a proper valuation subring containing $ℚ$, with none omitted at infinity. A divisor is a finitely supported integer function on all these places. Assume $h_{DVR}$ says each place ring is a discrete valuation ring. Write $o_P(f)$ for the negative logarithm of its maximal-ideal valuation (in particular $o_P(0)=0$), $\operatorname{div}(r)(P)=o_P(r)$, $\operatorname{pole}(f)(P)=\max(0,-o_P(f))$, and $\deg D=\sum_P D(P)[κ(P):ℚ]$, with the degrees computed by vector-space finrank. For every divisor $A$ with $0<\deg A$, there exist a natural number $n>0$ and actual elements $f,r∈K$ with $r≠0$ such that $\operatorname{pole}(f)=nA+\operatorname{div}(r)$ as divisors, hence coefficientwise at all places. There is no nonzero hypothesis on $f$, no uniqueness conclusion, no height hypothesis, and no residue-finiteness argument in the statement.

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.DegreeHeightMachine.chosenHeight_le_mul`

Let $N$ be any natural number and $M$ a model: its field $K$ is an intermediate field of an algebraic closure of $ℚ(T)$, with $u,v∈K$, $u$ transcendental over $ℚ$, $u^N+v^N=1$, $ℚ(u,v)=K$, and $K/ℚ(u)$ finite-dimensional of degree $N$. A place is a proper valuation subring containing $ℚ$, with none omitted at infinity. A divisor is a finitely supported integer function on all these places. Assume $h_{DVR}$ says each place ring is a discrete valuation ring. Write $o_P(f)$ for the negative logarithm of its maximal-ideal valuation (in particular $o_P(0)=0$), $\operatorname{div}(r)(P)=o_P(r)$, $\operatorname{pole}(f)(P)=\max(0,-o_P(f))$, and $\deg D=\sum_P D(P)[κ(P):ℚ]$, with the degrees computed by vector-space finrank. Also assume $h_{RF}$: every place’s residue field is finite-dimensional over $ℚ$. A point $x$ ranges over every pair of a place and a ring embedding of its entire residue field into $\overline{ℚ}$; neither an affine-open condition nor a bound on the full point-field degree is imposed. For each divisor $D$, choose a polar presentation $(f_D,g_D)$ whose coefficients satisfy $D(P)=\operatorname{pole}(f_D)(P)-\operatorname{pole}(g_D)(P)$ for every place. This is the choice made by `polarRep` from the nonempty type of such presentations. Define $H_D(x)=h_{(1,f_D)}(x)-h_{(1,g_D)}(x)$, where $h_s$ normalizes a finite tuple at $x.P$ by a nonzero entry of minimal order, evaluates through the residue embedding, and divides the relative logarithmic projective height by the degree of the field generated by all resulting coordinates; the zero tuple has height zero. The curve-field structure in scope means that $K/ℚ(t)$ is finite for some transcendental $t$. For arbitrary divisors $A,B$ and any real number $q$, assume $0<\deg B$ and $\deg A<q\deg B$ after casting degrees to $ℝ$. Then there exists $C∈ℝ$ such that $H_A(x)≤qH_B(x)+C$ for every point $x$. No positivity assumption is imposed on $q$; negative and zero $q$ are covered when the strict degree inequality holds. Equality of the two degrees in that inequality is not included. The real constant may depend on all fixed data and hypotheses, but is chosen before $x$ and is independent of $x$ and of its field degree; no nonnegativity or uniqueness of the constant is asserted. 

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.divisorDegreeHeightComparison`

Let $N$ be a natural number and let $F$ be an intermediate field between $\mathbb Q$ and an algebraic closure of $\mathbb Q(T)$, with elements $u,v$ such that $u$ is transcendental over $\mathbb Q$, $u^N+v^N=1$, $F=\mathbb Q(u,v)$, and $F$ is finite-dimensional of dimension $N$ over $\mathbb Q(u)$. A place $P$ means a valuation subring $O_P\ne F$ containing every rational number; write $k_P$ for its residue field. Assume every $O_P$ is a discrete valuation ring and every $k_P$ is finite-dimensional over $\mathbb Q$. For $f\in F$, put $o_P(f)=-\log_0(V_P(f))$, where $V_P$ is the valuation on $F$ from the maximal ideal of $O_P$ and $\log_0$ is the integer-valued total logarithm called `WithZero.log` in the code, and put $m_P(f)=\max(0,-o_P(f))$. A point $x$ consists of such a place $P_x$ and a ring homomorphism $\sigma_x:k_{P_x}\to\overline{\mathbb Q}$; for $f\in O_{P_x}$ write $f(x)=\sigma_x(\bar f)$, put $L_x=\sigma_x(k_{P_x})$ and $d_x=[L_x:\mathbb Q]$. For an algebraic number $z$, write $h(z)=\operatorname{logHeight}_1(z\text{ viewed in }\mathbb Q(z))/\deg(\mu_z)$, where $\mu_z$ is its minimal polynomial over $\mathbb Q$. Set $H_f(x)=h(f(x))$ if $f\in O_{P_x}$ and $H_f(x)=0$ otherwise. A presentation $R=(f,g)$ of a divisor $B$ means $B(P)=m_P(f)-m_P(g)$ at every place, and its height is $h_R(x)=H_f(x)-H_g(x)$; zero functions and common poles are not excluded. For every pair of finite-support integer-valued functions $D,E$ on the places, every presentation $R_D$ of $D$, every presentation $R_E$ of $E$, and every real $q$, if $\deg D=\sum_P D(P)[k_P:\mathbb Q]>0$ and $\deg E=\sum_P E(P)[k_P:\mathbb Q]<q\deg D$, then there exists $C\in\mathbb R$ such that $h_{R_E}(x)\le qh_{R_D}(x)+C$ for every point $x$. The degree inequality is strict; no sign assumption on $q$, no effectiveness assumption on $D,E$, no restriction to affine points, and no pole-avoidance condition is present, so the stipulated zero heights at poles remain part of the conclusion.

任意の自然数 $N$ とモデル $M$ を取る。その体 $K$ は $ℚ(T)$ の代数閉包の中間体であり、元 $u,v∈K$ は $u$ が $ℚ$ 上超越的、$u^N+v^N=1$、$ℚ(u,v)=K$ を満たし、$K/ℚ(u)$ は次数がちょうど $N$ の有限次元拡大である。素点は $ℚ$ を含む真の付値部分環で、無限遠の素点も除かない。因子はこれらすべての素点上の有限台を持つ整数値関数である。$h_{DVR}$ により各素点環が離散付値環であると仮定する。極大イデアルの付値の負の対数で定める位数を $o_P(f)$ と書き、特に $o_P(0)=0$ とする。$\operatorname{div}(r)(P)=o_P(r)$、$\operatorname{pole}(f)(P)=\max(0,-o_P(f))$、$\deg D=\sum_P D(P)[κ(P):ℚ]$ と定める。体の次数はベクトル空間の有限ランクで計算する。さらに $h_{RF}$ として、すべての素点の剰余体が $ℚ$ 上有限次元であると仮定する。点 $x$ は素点とその剰余体全体から $\overline{ℚ}$ への環埋め込みのすべての組を動き、アフィン開集合への制限も点の体全体の次数の上限も課さない。各因子 $D$ について、すべての素点で $D(P)=\operatorname{pole}(f_D)(P)-\operatorname{pole}(g_D)(P)$ を満たす極因子表示の非空な型から、`polarRep` により一組 $(f_D,g_D)$ を選ぶ。$H_D(x)=h_{(1,f_D)}(x)-h_{(1,g_D)}(x)$ と定める。$h_s$ は有限組を $x.P$ で位数最小の非零成分により正規化し、剰余体埋め込みを通して評価した座標の相対対数射影高さを、すべての座標が生成する体の次数で割った値である。零の組の高さは零とする。作用域内の曲線関数体構造は、ある超越元 $t$ に対し $K/ℚ(t)$ が有限であることを意味する。任意の因子 $A,B$ と任意の実数 $q$ に対し、$0<\deg B$ および、次数を実数に写したとき $\deg A<q\deg B$ を仮定する。ある $C∈ℝ$ が存在し、すべての点 $x$ で $H_A(x)≤qH_B(x)+C$ となる。$q$ に正の条件はなく、厳密な次数不等式が成立すれば零や負の $q$ も含む。次数不等式が等号となる場合は含まない。実定数は固定したデータと仮定すべてに依存してよいが、$x$ より前に選ばれ、$x$ およびその体の次数には依存しない。定数の非負性や一意性は主張しない。

`AbcAdaptation.Tripod.Fermat.Proper.divisorDegreeHeightComparison`

自然数 $N$ に対し、$F$ を $\mathbb Q$ と $\mathbb Q(T)$ の代数閉包の間の中間体とし、$u,v\in F$ が、$u$ は $\mathbb Q$ 上超越的、$u^N+v^N=1$、$F=\mathbb Q(u,v)$、および $F$ は $\mathbb Q(u)$ 上有限次元でその次元は $N$、という条件を満たすとする。ここで素点 $P$ とは、すべての有理数を含み $F$ と異なる付値部分環 $O_P$ をいい、その剰余体を $k_P$ と書く。すべての $O_P$ が離散付値環であり、すべての $k_P$ が $\mathbb Q$ 上有限次元であると仮定する。$f\in F$ に対し $o_P(f)=-\log_0(V_P(f))$ と置く。ただし $V_P$ は $O_P$ の極大イデアルによる $F$ 上の付値、$\log_0$ はコードで `WithZero.log` と呼ばれる整数値の全域的対数である。また $m_P(f)=\max(0,-o_P(f))$ と置く。点 $x$ は、そのような素点 $P_x$ と環準同型 $\sigma_x:k_{P_x}\to\overline{\mathbb Q}$ の組である。$f\in O_{P_x}$ のとき $f(x)=\sigma_x(\bar f)$ と書き、$L_x=\sigma_x(k_{P_x})$、$d_x=[L_x:\mathbb Q]$ と置く。代数的数 $z$ に対し、$\mathbb Q$ 上の最小多項式を $\mu_z$ とし、$h(z)=\operatorname{logHeight}_1(z\text{ を }\mathbb Q(z)\text{ の元とみなす})/\deg(\mu_z)$ と書く。$f\in O_{P_x}$ のとき $H_f(x)=h(f(x))$、それ以外のとき $H_f(x)=0$ と置く。因子 $B$ の表示 $R=(f,g)$ とは各素点で $B(P)=m_P(f)-m_P(g)$ が成り立つことをいい、その高さを $h_R(x)=H_f(x)-H_g(x)$ とする。零関数や共通の極は排除されていない。素点上の任意の有限台の整数値関数 $D,E$、それぞれの任意の表示 $R_D,R_E$、および任意の実数 $q$ に対し、$\deg D=\sum_P D(P)[k_P:\mathbb Q]>0$ かつ $\deg E=\sum_P E(P)[k_P:\mathbb Q]<q\deg D$ ならば、実数 $C$ が存在し、すべての点 $x$ で $h_{R_E}(x)\le qh_{R_D}(x)+C$ が成り立つ。次数の不等式は厳密であり、$q$ の符号や $D,E$ の有効性は仮定しない。点をアフィン点に限る条件も極の回避条件もないので、極で零と定義した高さも結論に含まれる。
